summary: Feed s051_single to APM is degraded due to VXLAN encapsulation: 61.2% (1722/2813) frames are tunneled. All other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, drops, overload, truncated, oversize, VLAN, encrypted share) are healthy, but APM cannot parse inner flows while encapsulated.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic (1722 frames) without decapsulation/stripping. APM is receiving the overlay (outer VTEP headers) instead of the inner tenant Ethernet/IP/TCP headers, indicating missing 'strip VXLAN header' policy on the broker ingress/egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees only outer tunnel headers and cannot decode inner application transactions, TCP handshakes, or latency metrics. With 61.2% of traffic opaque, application performance monitoring, transaction tracing, and error detection are blind for majority of flows despite APM not requiring full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping VXLAN at the packet broker exposes inner L2-L4 headers so APM can correlate flows and measure application latency without needing to understand overlay encapsulation.
